title: A position paper argues language models still lack science’s abductive leap
friendlyTitle: A researcher asks whether AI can make the creative jump behind new science
summary: Google DeepMind researcher Tom Zahavy argues that language models are increasingly capable at induction and deduction but lack the abductive step that forms new explanatory hypotheses. Using Einstein’s development of general relativity as a case study, the paper proposes physically consistent multimodal world models as a possible bridge.
friendlySummary: The paper says language models can find patterns and follow logic, but may still struggle to invent a completely new explanation. It suggests AI may need stronger models of the physical world.
whyItMatters: The paper offers a useful counterweight to claims that stronger theorem proving automatically produces general scientific invention. It is a conceptual position, not experimental proof of a permanent limit, but it helps teams separate generating and checking solutions from deciding which new questions or explanations deserve pursuit.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Being good at proofs is not the same as choosing a new scientific idea. This is an argument, not a proven limit, but it explains why human curiosity and judgement still matter.
